summary: Admitting a duplicate or lower-position copy of a run's claim no longer fails with a UNIQUE error on local_escalation_pending_v1: the escalation triggers skip an existing pending row with NOT EXISTS, since a position upsert's ON CONFLICT overrides the OR IGNORE inside the triggers it fires

replay.detail: No replay and no background work. Open moves the rows an older build left in local_escalation_pending_v1, normally none, in one statement.

schema.detail: Adds the host-local table local_escalation_pending_v2; no column or index change and no storage version change. The five escalation triggers become local_escalation_*_v2 and queue into local_escalation_pending_v2, skipping an existing pending row with NOT EXISTS instead of INSERT OR IGNORE, because an UPSERT's ON CONFLICT overrides the conflict policy of the triggers it fires: record_position_tx's position upsert raised UNIQUE for a claim already pending. Open drops the v1 triggers and moves any rows left in local_escalation_pending_v1 into local_escalation_pending_v2.

rules.detail: Verdicts are unchanged. The same receipts become pending as before; only the failing upsert now succeeds.

compatibility.detail: No wire, digest, capability or synced-table change. Escalation tables and triggers are host-local.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is supported. That release recreates its v1 triggers beside the v2 ones; they queue into separate tables (v1 into local_escalation_pending_v1, which that release reads, v2 into local_escalation_pending_v2), so the previous release behaves exactly as it did alone, whatever order SQLite fires them in, and no trigger checks which others exist. A test runs plain inserts, updates and deletes, position upserts with and without a pending row, with v1 created before and after v2, and compares each outcome and the pending rows it leaves with v1 alone. The previous release keeps its own fault: an upsert that moves a pending claim's position still fails there. Opening this release again drops v1, takes over the rows v1 queued, and every write succeeds. Rows v2 queued while the previous release ran are evaluated then.
